constraint_decided_it: No domain/range clause separated them -- both stay inside P14 (E7 -> E39, many to many necessary 1,n:0,n) on an E11 Modification, which is a subclass of E7, and E11's scope note explicitly covers 'the conservation treatment of an object'. They were separated on citation fidelity and on P11's scope note. B asserts that 'SIG Issue 488 confirms the general pattern of an actor acting at another's behest is handled by subtyping P14.1 in the role of'; the register's own outcome text says only that the SIG 'reviewed HW by GB - a proposal about subtyping P14.1 in the role of', that 'the alternative is to close the issue and revise it once CRMsoc has been addressed and decided upon', and 'Issue closed' -- a deferral to CRMsoc, not a confirmation, and its single archive thread (t1683) contains nothing but a link to Bruseker's slides. B also rejects P11 for the museum officer on the ground that P11 'is for actors whose participation, though not causal, is still a necessary part of the event itself'; P11's scope note imposes no necessity condition -- it says only 'active or passive participation ... does not imply any causal relationship'. That invented condition is what pushes B to P12, whereas t1546, the thread B cites, ends with Sanderson's 'Thus, as it's not P14, we should use P11 had participant' and Doerr's 'Yes, indeed!'.
better_modelling: One E11 Modification, P31 has modified the six E22 cabinets, with P14 carried out by to each of the two apprentices (P14.1 role: executant/conservator) and to the studio principal (P14.1 role: supervisor) -- exactly the shape of P14's own example, 'carried out by Michelangelo Buonaroti in the role of master craftsman', and licensed by Doerr's t1546 note that participants who are 'legally co-responsible' without acting 'should rather use P14'. Neither answer took the further step both are entitled to: the invoice makes the workshop itself, an E74 Group and hence an E39 Actor, the legally responsible party, so it should also carry P14 alongside the named individuals rather than being treated only as a rejected alternative. For the museum's conservation officer, A's first option is the right one -- her two visits are her own E7 inspection activities, P14 carried out by her, related to the treatment temporally rather than asserted as part of it. If a direct link to the E11 is wanted instead, P11 had participant (range E39) is the more specific term than P12 occurred in the presence of (range E77) for an Actor, and it is the term t1546 actually settled on for the not-P14 case.
reasoning: Both answers reach the modelling the CRM prescribes: E11 Modification (its scope note names conservation treatment), P14 to principal and apprentices distinguished by P14.1, and no P14 for the museum officer, and both correctly note that P14.1 has no standalone identifier and appears only inside P14's declaration and its FOL clause P14(x,y,z) => [P14(x,y) ^ E55(z)]. A's two quotations verify verbatim in t1546 and t1477; B's t1546 quotation verifies too, but its Issue 488 claim does not -- the issue was closed pending CRMsoc, so 'confirms' attributes a settlement the register does not record, which is unsupported under the rubric even though B's conclusion is right. A is additionally cleaner on the officer, offering her separate monitoring acts before falling back to P12, while B forecloses P11 by adding a necessity requirement that P11's scope note does not contain. A's one weakness is calling t1477 a thread that 'reserves' the workshop-of pattern for unknown doers, when that thread is an unresolved two-message question -- but the substance A attributes to it is present verbatim in Sanderson's text, so it overstates status rather than inventing content.
